rationale: Reflects the final implementation as of the tri-state refactor (commit 83f85e81e) and the MR-review round that followed it. All three findings from code-review-final.json are resolved, and three further items raised during MR review are resolved on top of them. The readiness result is now a tri-state (configured / not_configured / not_checked) rather than a boolean, so no provider the check does not actually validate is reported as configured. LiteLLM proxy activation matches the chat runtime criteria exactly. The AWS credential lookup is bounded and an unresolvable chain reports not_checked rather than asserting credentials are absent. The `missing` array served on the unauthenticated /v1/healthcheck contains configuration setting names only, never configured values. The chat path is untouched: core/dependecies.py, llm_service.py and enterprise/litellm/* are not in the diff.

business_review.item: AC10: operator supplies credentials for a single hosted provider (Azure OpenAI or AWS Bedrock) and configures nothing else -> app starts, chat works via that provider
business_review.notes: Diff does not touch the chat path. The readiness check derives the provider from llm_service.get_default_model_for_category(GLOBAL) and validates the exact settings named in the spec. Runtime verification of the 'chat works' half is manual — see qa-report.md.

business_review.item: AC10 Negative: no model provider configured -> app still starts and names the missing configuration, rather than silently presenting a working product that fails on first chat
business_review.notes: Every native branch (no default model / Azure / Bedrock / unset provider) warns at startup and reports not_configured with the missing setting names. The LiteLLM branch now requires is_litellm_enabled() AND config.LLM_PROXY_MODE == 'lite_llm' (model_provider_readiness.py:112), matching llm_factory.py:1083-1088 and 1137-1142, so LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=true with the default internal mode falls through to native validation instead of falsely reporting litellm_proxy. CR-003 resolved.

business_review.item: "What configured means": MODELS_ENV selects a profile file that loads
business_review.notes: Explicitly out of scope per plan.md Global Constraints — the YAML load happens at import time via the llm_config singleton and a failure there already crashes the process before lifespan() runs.

business_review.item: "What configured means": profile contains >=1 enabled chat model, and a GLOBAL default model exists
business_review.notes: Reuses llm_service.get_default_model_for_category(ModelCategory.GLOBAL), which filters on model.enabled and is_default_for(GLOBAL). Absence reports not_configured with MISSING_GLOBAL_DEFAULT_MODEL (model_provider_readiness.py:54, 118-124).

business_review.item: "What configured means": Azure OpenAI credentials = AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY and AZURE_OPENAI_URL both present
business_review.notes: Azure branch checks both through _is_present(), which strips before testing, so a whitespace-only value counts as missing per the ticket's 'nonblank' wording. Dedicated tests for missing key, missing url, and both present.

business_review.item: "What configured means": AWS Bedrock = region resolvable plus credentials resolvable through the standard boto3 credential chain
business_review.notes: _check_aws_bedrock_configured() (model_provider_readiness.py:79) resolves the region through _bedrock_session(), which passes AWS_BEDROCK_REGION when supplied and None otherwise, matching get_bedrock_runtime_client() at core/dependecies.py:173-180. Credentials come from session.get_credentials(), so IRSA, EKS Pod Identity, ECS/container credentials, shared config and IMDS all satisfy the check; no static access keys are required. The Bedrock model API is never called. The earlier _has_resolvable_aws_credentials() helper was folded into this function so one session serves both lookups.

business_review.item: A configuration that satisfies credentials but not the selected profile (e.g. AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY set while MODELS_ENV=aws) must be reported not configured
business_review.notes: Credential checks key off the selected profile's actual default_model.provider, not off which env vars happen to be set. Covered end to end by test_models_env_aws_with_only_azure_credentials_reports_missing_bedrock_configuration.

business_review.item: Providers beyond Azure/Bedrock (google_vertexai, anthropic, vertex_ai-anthropic_models) must not be falsely reported as configured or not_configured
business_review.notes: The fallback branch returns status=not_checked with the provider named (model_provider_readiness.py:152-156). Their existing runtime behavior is unchanged. Tested.

business_review.item: LiteLLM proxy active (is_litellm_enabled() AND LLM_PROXY_MODE == 'lite_llm') is reported as not_checked with provider='litellm_proxy', without inspecting or altering LiteLLM configuration
business_review.notes: model_provider_readiness.py:112-118 returns exactly that. Nothing about the LiteLLM runtime is read or validated.

business_review.item: A failure inside the readiness check itself reports not_checked, not not_configured, with only a sanitized reason in the health output
business_review.notes: Two layers. _check_aws_bedrock_configured() returns not_checked with UNRESOLVED_AWS_CREDENTIALS when the credential chain raises (model_provider_readiness.py:90-98), preserving any region finding alongside it. main.py:296-306 wraps the whole check and degrades to not_checked with 'model provider readiness check failed; see startup logs'. Both send the exception to logger.exception only.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: never log or return secret values, only setting names
business_review.notes: No credential value is read into any message. Beyond that, every entry in the `missing` array is a fixed module-level constant (model_provider_readiness.py:51-55) with no interpolation at all, so the MODELS_ENV value and the default model's base_name no longer reach the unauthenticated /v1/healthcheck; both remain in the startup log via logger.warning at model_provider_readiness.py:121 and 146. Asserted by test_no_global_default_model_reports_not_configured, test_unset_provider_reports_not_configured, and the two matching startup-log tests.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: /healthcheck HTTP status code stays 200 in all cases
business_review.notes: No status_code override. healthcheck() reads app.state through getattr(..., None) with an 'unknown' fallback (common.py:60-68), so mounting the router without main.py's lifespan cannot turn a Kubernetes probe endpoint into a 500. All three probes target /v1/healthcheck per deploy-templates/values.yaml:506,517,532. Four tests assert 200 across configured, not_configured, not_checked and unset-state responses. CR-002 resolved.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: no outbound call to a provider model API at startup; credential resolution may contact STS or metadata endpoints
business_review.notes: Corrected from the original plan's stronger and inaccurate 'no outbound calls' wording. No Azure or Bedrock model API is called. The AWS credential chain can legitimately reach container metadata or IMDS. The IMDS leg is pinned to metadata_service_timeout=1 and metadata_service_num_attempts=1 on the session (model_provider_readiness.py:60-61, 68-84), botocore's own defaults, which are otherwise overridable through AWS_METADATA_SERVICE_TIMEOUT and AWS_METADATA_SERVICE_NUM_ATTEMPTS. This is not an overall deadline for the chain and is not documented as one: those settings reach the instance-metadata provider only (botocore/credentials.py:93, botocore/utils.py:759), the ECS/EKS container fetcher uses botocore's fixed ContainerMetadataFetcher 2s x 3 attempts, and a credential_process profile runs an external command with no timeout. Assume-role and web-identity providers return DeferredRefreshableCredentials, so no STS call happens during this check. For the deployment shapes this ticket targets the practical worst case is a few seconds against a 600s startupProbe budget.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: the check must not load or re-parse llm-<MODELS_ENV>-config.yaml itself
business_review.notes: Only calls llm_service.get_default_model_for_category(), reusing the already-loaded llm_config singleton.

business_review.item: Compute readiness once at boot, store on app.state, log it, and surface it on GET /healthcheck without blocking startup
business_review.notes: Single call site at main.py:817 inside lifespan(), after LiteLLM model initialization so the check sees the same model catalog the chat path will use. Nothing recomputes it per request. test_lifespan_computes_model_provider_readiness_and_stores_it_on_app_state fails if that call site is removed. CR-001 resolved.

standards_review.notes: All commits use 'EPMCDME-14653: <Description>', matching the <TICKET-ID>: Short Description convention in .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md.

License headers present on all new files. The module uses typing.Optional[str] rather than X | None; verified not ruff-enforced (pyproject.toml ruff select list has no UP rules) and the prevailing convention across src/codemie/service/*.py, so not a blocking deviation. botocore is imported directly, following the existing precedent at core/dependecies.py:18 (from botocore.config import Config); it is already a boto3 dependency, not a new one.

Matches .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md secret handling: only setting names are logged or returned, never values. /v1/healthcheck was already unauthenticated before this change, so no new auth surface is introduced; the payload added to it was reduced during MR review to setting names only. See MR-002 and MR-004.

finding_status.notes: A bug in the readiness check can no longer abort startup. main.py:296-306 wraps check_model_provider_readiness() in try/except, logs via logger.exception, and degrades to status=NOT_CHECKED with the fixed reason 'model provider readiness check failed; see startup logs' — not_configured would have asserted something the check never established, and interpolating the exception text would have leaked internals onto the health endpoint. Verified by test_check_model_provider_readiness_swallows_exceptions_and_still_starts, which asserts the sanitized message and that 'boom' does not appear in it.

healthcheck() uses getattr(request.app.state, 'model_provider_readiness', None) with a {'status': 'unknown', 'provider': None, 'missing': []} fallback (common.py:60-68). Verified by test_healthcheck_never_500s_when_app_state_readiness_is_unset, which mounts the router on a bare FastAPI() with no lifespan and asserts 200.

The LiteLLM branch condition is now `is_litellm_enabled() and config.LLM_PROXY_MODE == "lite_llm"` (model_provider_readiness.py:112), and the branch reports not_checked rather than configured. test_litellm_enabled_but_internal_mode_falls_through_to_native_check asserts that LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=true with LLM_PROXY_MODE='internal' reaches the native branch instead of reporting litellm_proxy.

Raised in MR review: boto3.Session().get_credentials() can reach ECS container credentials or EC2 IMDS and runs synchronously inside lifespan(), so an unreachable metadata endpoint delays startup. Resolved two ways. _bedrock_session() (model_provider_readiness.py:68-84) pins metadata_service_timeout and metadata_service_num_attempts to 1 so no operator environment can widen the IMDS leg. Follow-up note from the same review: this is not an overall deadline for the credential chain, and the docstrings and plan.md were corrected to say so explicitly — the container fetcher and a credential_process profile carry their own separate (or absent) limits. Separately, a raised exception now reports not_checked with a sanitized reason instead of being recorded as missing credentials — a chain that fails to resolve establishes nothing. asyncio.to_thread was considered and rejected: lifespan() awaits the sequence either way, so it changes which thread blocks, not how long startup takes. Replacing the chain with a purely local environment probe was rejected because the ticket requires the standard boto3 credential chain and a local probe would report not_checked for every EC2 instance-role deployment.

Raised in MR review: the new model_provider object on the unauthenticated /v1/healthcheck exposed the MODELS_ENV value and the default model's base_name. Both interpolations were removed; every `missing` entry is now a fixed constant naming a configuration setting (model_provider_readiness.py:51-55). The dropped detail moved to logger.warning at model_provider_readiness.py:121 and 146, so operator diagnostics are preserved without widening the public response. No documentation MR is mechanically required: the route carries include_in_schema=False (common.py:54) and so is absent from the OpenAPI spec; the only repository references to the path are the three Helm probe entries in deploy-templates/README.md.

Raised in MR review: test_log_model_provider_readiness_never_logs_a_credential_value asserted that 'sk-super-secret-value' was absent from the log without ever placing that value anywhere, so the assertion could not fail. Replaced by test_a_configured_credential_value_never_reaches_the_log_or_the_health_payload, which sets AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY to that value and leaves AZURE_OPENAI_URL blank, then runs the real check_model_provider_readiness() plus log_model_provider_readiness() path. With a live secret in config it asserts the value appears in neither caplog.text nor any entry of the returned missing array, and that missing contains exactly ['AZURE_OPENAI_URL']. The implementation was already correct; only the test was vacuous.

Raised in cross-review: no test proved lifespan() actually invokes the readiness check — the helper-level tests all stayed green with the main.py:817 call site deleted. Separately, the lifespan tests executed the real check, which for a Bedrock-default profile resolves the live AWS credential chain. Both closed by test_lifespan_computes_model_provider_readiness_and_stores_it_on_app_state and by a _STUB_READINESS patch in the mock_non_litellm_startup fixture and the ExitStack lifespan test.
